name: Iron Oxide Black (CI 77499)
regulatory: FDA 21 CFR 73.2250 (color additive); EU Cosmetic Reg. Annex IV. Not a UV filter under FDA monograph but the most efficient single per-mass HEV blocker of the three iron-oxide colorants.
metric: E(1%, 1cm) -- effective mass attenuation (absorption + Mie scattering) for pigment-grade ~300 nm primary particles in cosmetic film. E1% = 10 x k(L/g/cm). Note: magnetite is semi-metallic so 'bandgap' is not well-defined; spectrum is broadband flat across 280-800 nm.
primary_sources: Schlegel, Alvarado, Wachter 1980 Philos Mag B 42:419 -- single-crystal magnetite reflectance 0.03-12 eV; reflectivity ~20-25% across visible, indicative of strong broadband absorption.
Querry 1985 (refractiveindex.info) -- magnetite n,k 0.21-55.6 um. In visible: n approx 2.4, k approx 0.5-1.0 (large imaginary part = strong absorption).
Morris et al. 1985 J Geophys Res 90:3126 -- magnetite powder reflectance is essentially flat ~5-8% across 400-2500 nm (definitive black appearance).

Cornell & Schwertmann 2003 'The Iron Oxides' (book) -- magnetite is semi-metallic above the Verwey transition (T > 120 K); inverse spinel structure with Fe2+/Fe3+ charge-transfer giving featureless broadband absorption.
Dumbuya et al. 2020 J Drugs Dermatol 19:712 -- iron-oxide blends; black is typically the smallest mass fraction (5-15%) but largest per-mass HEV contribution.
Ezekwe et al. 2024 PPP 40:e12937 -- 71.9-86% HEV blockade in iron-oxide blended formulations.
physical_notes: Magnetite is SEMI-METALLIC, not a semiconductor. There is no Tauc bandgap edge -- the spectrum is approximately FLAT across 280-800 nm and continues into the NIR. Do not try to fit a bandgap cutoff.
Charge-transfer between Fe2+ (3d6) and Fe3+ (3d5) on octahedral sublattice gives intervalence absorption that is essentially wavelength-independent through visible.
Refractive index n~2.4, extinction k~0.5-1.0 in visible -- both real and imaginary parts large -> strong reflection AND absorption. Gives black + slight metallic luster.

Per unit mass, magnetite is the MOST EFFICIENT of the three iron oxides at 400-500 nm because its absorption is broadband, not edge-limited. ~10-25% load of magnetite alone produces a near-opaque film; cosmetic uses keep it <2% to avoid grey/black appearance.

concentration_nonlinearity.model: f(c) = 1 - alpha * tanh(max(0, c - c0) / scale)
concentration_nonlinearity.rationale: Magnetite saturates VERY rapidly because per-particle attenuation is so high -- at 1% load + 1.3 mg/cm2 a film is already near-opaque. f(c) drops sharply.
concentration_nonlinearity.source: Empirical: Ezekwe 2024 reports >85% HEV blockade at <0.5% black-iron-oxide loadings in tinted SPF 35; if linearly extrapolated to 5% the prediction would be >99.99% which is consistent with observations of dark-tinted formulations reaching 98% blockade. Saturation is driven by film opacification.

particle_size_correction.model: multiplier on E1%(lambda); pigment-grade is the cosmetic norm
particle_size_correction.source: For a strongly-absorbing material (k~1) the optimum mass-specific extinction is at primary size near lambda/(2*pi*n) ~ 50-150 nm -- but magnetite pigment is typically supplied at 200-500 nm for color stability. Ultrafine magnetite (<30 nm) is superparamagnetic and used in MRI contrast, not cosmetics.

hev_model.absorbance: A(lambda) = E1%(lambda) x f(c) x g(d) x 100 x c_active_g_per_cm2
hev_model.near_opacity_warning: At c >= 1.5% the predicted HEV blockade exceeds 95% -- formulations at this loading appear visibly grey/black and are used only for camouflage cosmetics, not aesthetic tinted sunscreens.

validation.source: Inferred from Ezekwe 2024 / Dumbuya 2020 blend deconvolution
Colorescience / Ezekwe 2024 internal data on black iron oxide contribution
Camouflage cosmetic literature (Dermablend / Covermark style) -- 1% IO black gives near-complete HEV blockade alone

validation.formulation: Dark camouflage tint 2% IO Black, 2 mg/cm2
validation.source: Camouflage formulation literature; consistent with 'darker formulations enriched with higher concentrations of iron oxides reaching up to 98%' (Lyons 2021)

validation_summary.note: Black iron oxide validation is tight -- the broadband flat spectrum is well-characterized and there are fewer free parameters (no edge to fit).

caveats: Peak E1% = 95 is at 340-400 nm. Old chart value 1800 was overstated by ~20x. Magnetite is the strongest of the three IRON OXIDES per unit mass -- consistent with prior 1800 being highest of the three -- but still <1% of the overstated value.
Magnetite's spectrum is FLAT, not edge-shaped. Don't model it as a semiconductor with a bandgap.

Effective k INCLUDES Mie scattering and reflection losses (~20% reflectivity per Schlegel 1980). For a Beer-Lambert-style absorbance calculation this is acceptable -- the reflected portion is also 'blocked' light from the skin's perspective.
f(c) saturates very rapidly (alpha=0.85, scale=1.5) -- magnetite is the most aggressive saturator of the three. Loadings above 1% give diminishing returns and visible darkening of the product.

Cosmetic implications: black iron oxide is typically the smallest mass fraction in tinted sunscreens (e.g. 0.1-0.5%) yet contributes ~50% of HEV blockade. Formulators should treat it as the 'efficient' pigment.
Magnetite slowly oxidizes to maghemite (gamma-Fe2O3) on storage -- maghemite is brown not black; cosmetic formulations include antioxidants/encapsulation to preserve color.
